entries.title: Rewrite the ICX USB/LAN manuals as BNC documents, then restore the PDF downloads

notes.text: OPEN 2026-08-19, needs engineering + marketing. The three downloadable ICX USB/LAN manual PDFs were the original supplier documents, unmodified: supplier logo on the cover, supplier wordmark silkscreened on the product photos, and the supplier's own model numbers throughout. Two of the three were byte-identical and served under two different BNC filenames. They have been withdrawn from the site (files deleted, pdf-map entries removed, and the three PDF URLs 301 to their HTML manual pages), so no customer can download a supplier-branded document today. The HTML manuals themselves are fully rebranded and stay live. What is still needed: re-issue each manual as a genuine BNC document (BNC cover, BNC model numbers, product photography without the supplier wordmark, SpectraCore screenshots relabelled), then add the new PDFs back to docs/pdfs/ and re-register them in docs/pdfs/pdf-map.json so the download line and hero button return. Affected: bnc-icx-series-usb-lan-manual.html (was bnc-icx-fieldhawk-usb-san-manual.html and bnc-icx-usb-lan-san-nx-manual.html, now merged) and bnc-icx-series-usb-lan-20ghz-manual.html (was bnc-icx-usb-lan-sae-nxe-manual.html). verify.

OPEN 2026-08-19, needs engineering. Two model-coverage gaps remain after the all-models restore. (1) bnc-icx-fieldhawk-usb-datasheet.html has no ICX-045U row or column: its spec values were never recorded in the hidden markup, so they must come from the source datasheet rather than be inferred. (2) The ICX-090R to ICX-095R rename from 2026-08-13 is only half applied across the site, so the rugged line is described inconsistently. Confirm which name is current and it can be swept in one pass. verify.

entries.title: DEI High Power/Current Pulsers line page

notes.text: SEO sweep 2026-07-08 (verify): the page's previous meta description claimed 300 kV, but the page content says 30 kV max for DC supplies. Confirm the correct top-line voltage for the DEI line; the new meta avoids the number until engineering confirms.

Branding & verification notes. This manual is reconciled from the ICX-090 / ICX-200 series source documentation. The ICX-FieldHawk presents that measurement engine in a field-portable form factor. The following assumptions were applied; please confirm before publication. Form factor. The source document specifies the measurement-module hardware. It does not state handheld-specific mechanics (display size, battery life, ingress rating, drop rating). Those handheld attributes are therefore omitted rather than invented. verify. Model mapping. The numeric part is the maximum frequency in GHz times 10 and is preserved exactly. The three frequency variants map to ICX-090 (9 kHz to 9.5 GHz), ICX-200 (9 kHz to 20 GHz), and ICX-400 (9 kHz to 40 GHz). The ICX-400 (40 GHz) is part of the ICX-FieldHawk line; its specifications, including the 2.4 mm (M) RF input, are drawn from the 40 GHz product documentation. Software rename. The source control software is renamed throughout to SpectraCore, Berkeley Nucleonics' spectrum analysis firmware. Described functionality is unchanged. Antenna accessories. External antennas are presented as accessories drawn from the RFA-3100-N family. Confirm the part number. verify. Specifications. All spec values are reproduced identically from the source for the same measurement hardware. Tables were lightly regrouped for readability. Values remain preliminary pending verification against the published BNC datasheet. verify. In-software branding. The SpectraCore screenshots in sections 2 and 3 carry the source vendor wordmark masked from the application title bar. Recapture with the BNC / SpectraCore mark when available. verify.

Branding & verification notes. This manual is reconciled from the ICX-090 / ICX-200 series source documentation. The source documents two frequency variants over USB and networked interfaces. The assumptions below were applied; confirm each before publication. Model mapping. The numeric part is the maximum frequency in GHz times 10 and is preserved exactly. The line covers three bands: 9.5 GHz, 20 GHz, and 40 GHz. These map to ICX-090R (9 kHz to 9.5 GHz), ICX-200R (9 kHz to 20 GHz), and ICX-400R (9 kHz to 40 GHz). The R suffix marks the FieldHawk-R Field-Ready line. The 40 GHz ICX-400R RF specifications, including its 2.4 mm (M) RF input, are drawn from the 40 GHz product documentation; IP68 enclosure attributes remain to be confirmed. verify. Rugged-specific claims not in the source. The source documentation describes compact USB and networked modules. It does not state an IP68 rating, MIL-STD-810H qualification, a built-in display or touch screen, an internal battery, or an on-board AI compute platform. The 40 GHz ICX-400R and its 2.4 mm (M) RF input are taken from the 40 GHz product documentation. Any IP68 enclosure, connector, display, battery, or AI-platform specification for the FieldHawk-R must come from the FieldHawk-R hardware datasheet, not this source. verify. Software rename. The source control software is renamed throughout to SpectraCore, Berkeley Nucleonics' spectrum analysis firmware. Described functionality is unchanged. Specifications. All spec values are reproduced identically from the source for the same RF hardware. Tables were lightly regrouped for readability. Values remain preliminary pending verification against the published BNC datasheet. verify. In-software branding. The SpectraCore screenshots in sections 3 and 4 carry the SpectraCore mark in the application title bar, relabeled from the source vendor wordmark. Recapture against released firmware before publication. verify.

entries.title: ICX-Series USB & LAN Analyzer Manual | BNC

notes.text: Branding & verification notes. This Product Manual covers the Berkeley Nucleonics ICX-Series family of compact USB and networked real-time spectrum analyzers. The analysis software is SpectraCore. Model designators in the specification tables are BNC part numbers: the U suffix marks the USB-connected models and the N suffix their Gigabit-Ethernet equivalents, with -P denoting the Performance+ tier. All specification values, units, and tolerances are reproduced exactly from the source manual, with light reordering for readability only. Items to confirm, marked "verify": the BNC document and revision identifier against the source V1.0 / dc-51306202 (verify); the antenna part numbers under Options 34 and 35 if BNC assigns ANT-series codes such as RFA-3100-N (verify); and the SpectraCore release build strings quoted under Test Conditions (verify they carry to BNC release builds).

entries.title: ICX-Series/N Spectrum Analyzer Manual, 20 GHz | BNC

notes.text: Branding & verification notes. This manual is reconciled from the ICX-090 / ICX-200 series source documentation. The following assumptions were applied; please confirm before publication. Model numbering. The numeric part is the maximum frequency in GHz times 10, zero-padded to three digits. USB models belong to the ICX-Series and carry a U suffix (ICX-090U, ICX-200U). LAN / Ethernet models belong to ICX-FieldHawk-N and carry an N suffix (ICX-090N, ICX-200N). The "-N" LAN suffix is a proposed convention. verify. Software rename. The source control software is renamed throughout to SpectraCore, Berkeley Nucleonics' spectrum analysis firmware. Described functionality is unchanged. Antenna accessories. External antennas are presented as accessories, not options, drawn from the RFA-3100-N / RFA-3200-N family. Confirm the part number. verify. Specifications. All spec values are reproduced identically from the source for the same hardware. Tables were lightly regrouped for readability. Values remain preliminary pending verification against the published BNC datasheet. verify. In-software branding. The SpectraCore screenshots in sections 2 and 3 still show the source vendor wordmark in the application title bar. Relabel to the BNC / SpectraCore mark when the screenshots are recaptured. verify.
